structured_plan.G: Provisional G: retain the supplied correct baseline unchanged until research candidates are measured, integrated, and independently confirmed.
structured_plan.analysis: Choose N=3: the baseline is correct and measures 49.67 µs on average (three samples: 49.37–49.85 µs), while its byte-at-a-time ASCII scan and scalar multibyte decoding allow three distinct, testable approaches. Keep the primary 65,536-byte valid mixed-width workload as the performance objective; also require ASCII and malformed-input correctness. The compiler flags and effective ISA options are not provided, so any ISA-specific path must build and be measured on the stated target. Compare candidates on compatible measurements, and assess integrated combinations rather than assuming gains add.

children.objective: Explore a bulk ASCII-run fast path using safely loaded wide words or supported SIMD to identify non-ASCII bytes, then validate without reading past the input. Preserve a general scalar fallback and correct handling of tails and malformed sequences. Measure the primary mixed-width workload and ASCII case; verify malformed-input correctness and the complete output write.
children.subject: Wide ASCII-run skipping

children.objective: Explore blockwise SIMD validation of UTF-8 structure across the input, using byte classes and continuation/lead relationships while carrying boundary state between blocks. Enforce overlong, surrogate, maximum-code-point, and truncation rules, with safe tail handling and a valid fallback if needed. Build and measure on the stated target; check mixed-width performance and all correctness cases.
children.subject: SIMD structural UTF-8 validation

children.objective: Explore a non-SIMD, branch-reduced scalar validator such as a byte-class table or DFA, replacing the baseline’s code-point branches with per-byte state transitions. Preserve all Unicode scalar-value constraints and arbitrary input lengths. Measure the mixed-width workload and verify ASCII and malformed inputs, including truncated sequences.
children.subject: Branch-reduced scalar DFA
